description: Run JavaScript in this session's PERSISTENT runtime to look at and act on the GUI — web pages in a browser, Electron apps and native macOS apps, whichever this server mounts — the one tool for both. The code is an async function body: `await` every verb, `return` a value to get it back as JSON; top-level const/let/function declarations SURVIVE to later calls, so keep handles and collected data in them. Every verb lives on a surface HANDLE (a tab / window / app); there are no top-level verbs. Bind first: computer.surface('<id or title>') names one, computer.surface() alone takes the only surface or the one this session opened, computer.surfaces() lists them. Then w.observe() w.find(name) w.click(t) w.setText(t, text) w.keys(chord) w.scroll({…}) w.wait({…}) w.expect({…}) w.text() w.screenshot({…}) and this platform's own verbs (web pages: w.openUrl({url}), w.page({…}), …); a ref read on one surface is refused on another. The first bound operation claims the target across calls; await w.release() when its task is done. The first result carries the full API reference (computer.help() returns it again) — use only what it documents. One verb at a time: a failed action or expect() throws and stops the run; wait() returns false on timeout. expect() what the next step needs; return what you are checking. Per call: 100 actions, 60 s. No require/import/fetch/process/timers/console. Before an operation that may affect the user's foreground, real pointer, keyboard focus or system clipboard (including automatic fallback), explain its target and effects and get permission unless existing permission covers them; never silently escalate a background operation. Before sending a message or publishing a post, let the user confirm its content and recipients or destination, unless they already approved those exact details.

code.description: JavaScript, run as the body of an async function in the persistent runtime. `await` every verb; `return` what you want back. Bind once — first call: `const w = await computer.surface();` — binding opens nothing (a browser page is opened with `await w.openUrl({url})` once bound), then later calls use `w` directly: `for (const e of (await w.observe()).elements.filter(e => e.role === 'checkbox')) await w.click(e.ref);`

interaction.description: Native apps default to background — macOS: driver mouse/activation/clipboard routes are blocked, including fallback. Use desktop only after explaining effects and obtaining permission covering this call. This option is not user consent.

observation.description: How much of the end-of-run observation to render. "full" (default) is the element list and the text excerpt; "brief" keeps the head (title, targets, verdict) and drops the listing; "none" leaves only the action journal. The observation is always TAKEN either way — the change verdict and the stale-ref bookkeeping are unaffected — and a NOTE line always survives, so a swallowed click is never hidden by this. Reach for it when the window holds content you do not want in the transcript, or when your own `return` value is the answer.

platform.description: For a HOST that mounts several platforms in one session: the platform this call is about ("browser", "electron", "macos"). computer.surfaces() and computer.surface() then see only its surfaces, and the observation is of it; the other platforms stay mounted and untouched.

purpose.description: Briefly describe the intended task when requesting app access. Shown to the user as the agent's stated purpose; it does not narrow the app permission. Do not include secrets.

target.description: Bind this surface before the code runs — the same string computer.surface() takes (an id, a whole title, or a piece of one). For a HOST that decides which surface a call is about: the code can still bind whatever it likes; this settles where a run that binds nothing lands, and what computer.surface() with no argument returns in this call.

name: computer_repl
